issues.subcategory: Non-independence of dyadic observations
issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs, receive mutual misinformation, discuss jointly, and are randomized at the pair level, but the planned ANOVA appears to treat 240 individual participants as independent observations. Responses from members of the same dyad are likely correlated because they interact, influence each other, share session-level conditions, and have complementary stimulus versions. Ignoring clustering can underestimate standard errors, inflate Type I error, and invalidate power calculations. The analysis should model dyad as a random effect or otherwise account for pair-level dependence, and power should be based on the effective number of independent units for between-condition effects.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). ... Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups ... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels ... and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.subcategory: Power analysis ignores clustering/randomization unit
issues.description: The between-subjects manipulation is assigned to pairs, not individuals, yet the power analysis uses participant-level sample size and a standard repeated-measures ANOVA. Because the intervention is delivered at the dyad/session level, the relevant independent units for the between-group component are dyads, with two observations per cluster. Unless dyadic correlation is negligible and modeled appropriately, the claimed power for intervention effects is overstated.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups ... Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

issues.subcategory: Inappropriate ANOVA for bounded count outcomes
issues.description: The primary outcomes are counts from only eight critical items, and discussed/non-discussed item sets include only four critical details each. These outcomes are discrete, bounded, likely non-normal, and may have floor/ceiling effects. A standard repeated-measures ANOVA on counts or proportions can produce biased estimates and invalid inference, particularly with small item numbers and unequal exposure to misinformation. A binomial/multinomial generalized mixed model at the item level would better account for item difficulty, participant clustering, dyadic clustering, and response category structure.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details ... Four indices will be derived ... the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.subcategory: Item effects not modeled
issues.description: Only eight critical details are used, with four discussed and four non-discussed per participant depending on counterbalancing. Critical details may differ substantially in salience, memorability, confusability, and likelihood of discussion. The proposed analysis aggregates over items and does not include item as a random effect or fixed blocking factor, limiting generalizability beyond the specific items and potentially confounding discussion status with item difficulty if counterbalancing or randomization is imperfect.
issues.quote: Both versions are identical except for eight critical details ... 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs ... The correctness of answers to questions concerning discussed and non-discussed details will be compared.

issues.subcategory: Ambiguous and potentially incorrect conversion of effect size
issues.description: The manuscript converts a synthesized Hedges' g of 1.13 to Cohen's f of about 0.57 for a repeated-measures comparison, but does not describe the formula or whether the within-person correlation and paired nature of the effect were incorporated. For within-subject effects, conversions from standardized mean differences to f depend on the definition of the standardized difference and the repeated-measures correlation. This makes the power estimate for replication difficult to evaluate and potentially incorrect.
issues.quote: Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57. The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07. Under such conditions, the sample size required for 90% power was 18.

issues.subcategory: Meta-analysis based on two highly heterogeneous effects
issues.description: The replication power calculation synthesizes only two prior studies with very different effect sizes, Hedges' g = 1.92 and g = 0.38, and then uses the pooled estimate as if it were a stable expected effect. With only two studies, random-effects variance is extremely imprecise and the pooled effect is not a reliable planning value. This is especially problematic because the planned study modifies the final test from forced-choice to open-ended questions, so prior effects may not apply.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 ... and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 ... Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.subcategory: No manipulation checks for intervention uptake or mechanism
issues.description: The study makes mechanistic claims that interventions should alter awareness of discrepancies, source monitoring, confidence, motivation, alertness, and reliance on own memory, but no manipulation checks are specified to assess whether participants attended to, understood, believed, or were affected by the podcasts/DRM manipulation. Without such checks, null results or between-intervention differences will be difficult to interpret, and mediation claims about mechanisms will be unsupported.
issues.quote: Extended warning ... should make the participants who are aware of discrepancies discard the consistency assumption and make them rely on their own correct memories. ... Education about memory ... should prompt them to rethink their own memories ... Demonstration and motivation ... should make the participants alert to the real possibility that their reports may be distorted

issues.subcategory: Interventions are confounded and not construct-pure
issues.description: The three interventions are intended to represent distinct constructs—warning, education, and demonstration/motivation—but they overlap substantially in content and likely differ on multiple uncontrolled dimensions, including explicitness of deception, relevance to the task, motivational intensity, demand characteristics, interactivity, experimenter involvement, emotional salience, and duration. Therefore, any observed differences cannot be attributed cleanly to the named constructs.
issues.quote: we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation.

issues.subcategory: Extended warning combines multiple active components
issues.description: The extended warning is not simply a warning; it includes education about the misinformation effect, source monitoring instruction, confidence-related messaging, and full enlightenment about the deception. Because multiple active ingredients are bundled together, the study cannot identify whether effects are due to warning, education, social discrediting, source-monitoring instruction, demand characteristics, or disclosure of the study deception.
issues.quote: the following ideas were included ... a clear warning ... an extensive lecture on the nature of the misinformation effect ... information about the possibility of confusing sources of information ... information that many people ... give answers consistent with external sources ... an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.subcategory: Control condition is poorly matched
issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast about soft skills related to social attitudes, but the manuscript does not establish that it is matched to experimental conditions for length, interest, arousal, task relevance, credibility, demand characteristics, experimenter interaction, or cognitive load. It is especially unmatched to the Demonstration and motivation condition, which includes an interactive DRM task plus feedback and a motivational podcast. Differences may reflect attention, arousal, demand, or time-on-task rather than the intended intervention.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: Intervention duration not equated
issues.description: The Extended warning and Education podcasts are approximately seven minutes, but the Demonstration and motivation condition includes a DRM procedure, feedback, and a podcast, with no total duration specified. Unequal duration and cognitive engagement can confound intervention efficacy with elapsed time, rehearsal prevention, fatigue, or depth of processing.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... First ... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used ... Next, the participants’ motivation ... will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.subcategory: Mechanistic causal claims not testable with proposed measures
issues.description: The introduction predicts that interventions reduce conformity by affecting informational influence, discrepancy awareness, source monitoring, and confidence, but the analysis plan does not measure these processes directly. Observed changes in accuracy could arise from demand characteristics, general caution, response withholding, memory decay, or guessing rather than the theorized mechanisms. Causal claims about mechanisms should be avoided or tested with appropriate measures.
issues.quote: Our hypotheses are related mainly to informational influence ... This, naturally, relates only to participants who are aware of the inconsistencies ... we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies

issues.subcategory: Awareness of discrepancies is central but not measured prospectively
issues.description: The theory repeatedly states that the interventions should work primarily for participants aware of discrepancies between their memory and the co-witness information. However, the study does not include a direct, pre-test measure of discrepancy awareness or source memory before the intervention/final test. The later disputed/non-disputed discussion coding is not equivalent to internal awareness, and final responses cannot disentangle awareness from memory or demand effects.
issues.quote: we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.subcategory: DRM false recall does not demonstrate social influence or memory conformity
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention is motivated by inoculation against social influence and memory conformity, but the DRM task demonstrates associative false memory in individual recall, not vulnerability to co-witness misinformation or social influence. This mismatch weakens construct validity: the manipulation may alter beliefs about memory fallibility generally, but it does not directly demonstrate susceptibility to another witness’s influence.
issues.quote: in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used

issues.subcategory: Demand characteristics introduced by explicit disclosure
issues.description: The Extended warning and Demonstration/motivation conditions explicitly tell participants that the partner may have provided wrong information or that they should not rely on the partner. Such instructions may cue the desired response strategy and hypothesis, making reductions in misinformation responses potentially reflect compliance with perceived experimental demands rather than genuine resistance or memory protection.
issues.quote: The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner.

issues.subcategory: Post-randomization exclusion and replacement based on hypothesis guessing
issues.description: Participants who guess the hypotheses will be excluded and replaced to maintain sample size. This post-randomization exclusion can bias treatment comparisons, especially because the authors expect exclusions to differ by condition and because guessing may be an effect of the intervention itself. Replacing excluded participants also complicates the estimand and inflates researcher degrees of freedom unless strict rules are preregistered and analyses include both intention-to-treat and per-protocol approaches.
issues.quote: If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size. We realize that this may result in more exclusion in the three experimental groups than in the control group

issues.subcategory: Vague exclusion criterion for hypothesis awareness
issues.description: The manuscript does not specify how 'correctly guesses our hypotheses' will be operationalized, who will code responses, whether coders will be blind to condition, whether partial guesses count, or whether reliability will be assessed. Because exclusions are likely condition-dependent, ambiguous coding creates substantial analytic flexibility and potential bias.
issues.quote: the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis

issues.subcategory: Vague technical-problem exclusion criterion
issues.description: Participants will be excluded for 'any technical problems,' but technical failures in a MORI setup can vary in severity and detectability. Without predefined criteria, documentation procedures, and blinding of exclusion decisions to outcomes/condition, this creates analytic flexibility and potential selective exclusion.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: No missing data plan
issues.description: The manuscript does not specify how missing responses, skipped items, inaudible discussion recordings, incomplete sessions, dropout, or unusable confidence ratings will be handled. Because outcomes are counts over few items, missingness can materially affect accuracy estimates. Treating no response as incorrect, excluding items, or excluding participants can yield different conclusions.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: Insufficient scoring protocol for open-ended responses
issues.description: The final memory test uses open-ended questions, but the manuscript does not provide a detailed coding manual, allowable synonyms, spelling/tolerance rules, handling of ambiguous or multiple answers, coder training, number of coders, blinding to condition/discussion status, or interrater reliability. Open-ended scoring is subjective and central to the primary outcome, so replicability and validity require explicit coding procedures.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers

issues.subcategory: Potential lack of blinding in data collection and coding
issues.description: The study does not indicate whether experimenters administering interventions, conducting sessions, transcribing discussions, or coding open-ended responses will be blind to condition and hypotheses. Because interventions are obvious and outcome coding is subjective, lack of blinding could influence participant behavior, prompting, transcription, coding, and exclusion decisions.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded. ... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test ... We will exclude participants ...

issues.subcategory: Randomization procedure unspecified
issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs will be randomly assigned to groups but does not describe the randomization method, allocation concealment, blocking/stratification, balance across counterbalancing version, sex, familiarity, or stimulus version. Without these details, it is difficult to assess whether group assignment prevents systematic confounding.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.subcategory: Uncontrolled participant familiarity and relationship status
issues.description: Memory conformity is known to be affected by familiarity, trust, intimacy, dominance, and social relationship between co-witnesses. The recruitment and pairing procedure does not specify whether participants are strangers, acquaintances, friends, or couples, nor how familiarity will be measured or controlled. This can add variability or confound condition effects if pair composition differs across groups.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet. ... the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.

issues.subcategory: Uncontrolled demographic and social dynamics within dyads
issues.description: The study acknowledges age-related confounding but does not address other dyadic factors that can shape conformity, such as gender composition, dominance, confidence, social status, visual acuity, prior knowledge, or whether participants know each other. Without balancing or measuring these variables, intervention effects may be obscured or confounded.
issues.quote: The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one ... In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.

issues.subcategory: Eligibility criteria incomplete
issues.description: The sample is age-restricted, but no criteria are given for language proficiency, visual acuity/color vision, hearing, neurological/psychiatric conditions, medication, prior participation in memory studies, or familiarity with the MORI/DRM paradigms. These factors can affect encoding, perception of critical details, response to podcasts, and false recall.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: Possible inclusion of minors without consent procedures
issues.description: The sample includes 16- and 17-year-olds, but the manuscript does not describe parental consent/guardian permission, assent procedures, or ethical safeguards for minors exposed to deception and forensic/criminal material. This is a methodological and ethical reporting gap.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old

issues.subcategory: Ethics approval and consent not reported
issues.description: The study involves deception, covertly showing different films, audio recording discussions, and possibly minors, yet no ethics approval, informed consent, deception justification, recording consent, data protection, or debriefing content is described beyond a brief statement. These details are necessary to evaluate feasibility and ethical compliance.
issues.quote: Finally, the participants will be debriefed.

issues.subcategory: Tense and manuscript type inconsistency
issues.description: The manuscript alternates between presenting itself as a proposal/registered report and as a completed study. While not fatal, this creates ambiguity about whether procedures are planned, already conducted, or results are expected, and affects interpretation of the 'Results' section, which is actually an analysis plan.
issues.quote: The present research concerns such a problem ... The main goal of this proposal is to analyze ... The study will be conducted in 2023. If the Stage 1 review is accepted

issues.subcategory: Contradictory description of movie identity
issues.description: The procedure states that due to the MORI technique the recording will be identical for each person except for eight critical details. Strictly, each person sees a different version, not an identical recording. The wording is confusing and could obscure exactly what is manipulated.
issues.quote: Due to the technical manipulations of the MORI technique, the recording will be identical for each person in each pair, except for eight critical details.

issues.subcategory: Mismatch between stated collaborative recognition and open-ended final test
issues.description: The manuscript describes the collaborative phase as a recognition test with five possible responses, but the final test is open-ended. Prior MORI scoring rules and power estimates are based on forced-choice recognition. The change in response format is acknowledged but its implications for comparability, chance performance, response bias, and scoring are not fully addressed.
issues.quote: the participants will complete the collaborative recognition test. ... Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed ... Immediately after ... they will complete the individual memory test ... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions

issues.subcategory: Primary conformity operationalization conflates memory conformity with generic inaccuracy
issues.description: The proposed efficacy criterion is a smaller difference in accuracy between discussed and non-discussed items. This captures reduced accuracy costs for discussed items but does not distinguish adoption of co-witness misinformation from other errors, omissions, or conservative responding. Because interventions may increase 'don't know' or reduce overall responding, accuracy differences alone may not reflect memory conformity. The misinformation-consistent response rate should be a primary outcome or modeled jointly with correct/other/no-answer categories.
issues.quote: The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller in the group in which this method was applied than in the control group.

issues.subcategory: Multiple outcomes without multiplicity control
issues.description: The analysis plan proposes ANOVAs on four indices plus average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, follow-up pairwise comparisons, and exploratory DRM prediction. It does not define a single primary outcome or control the familywise error rate/false discovery rate. Multiple testing increases the chance of false-positive findings and allows selective emphasis on favorable outcomes.
issues.quote: We will explore ... using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices ... Moreover, we will observe ... average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions. ... follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed. As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor

issues.subcategory: Primary endpoint not clearly specified
issues.description: The manuscript identifies several possible dependent variables but does not clearly specify which index is primary for confirming the memory conformity effect and the intervention effect. Ambiguity among correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, total answers, and accuracy enables outcome switching and selective interpretation.
issues.quote: using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.subcategory: Follow-up comparison plan incomplete
issues.description: The plan states that pairwise follow-up comparisons will be performed if the general interaction is significant, but it does not specify which comparisons are confirmatory, how multiple comparisons will be adjusted, whether tests are one- or two-sided consistently, or whether the hypothesized ordering among the three interventions will be tested. This limits preregistration clarity.
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.subcategory: Conditioning pairwise tests on omnibus interaction may miss planned effects
issues.description: The authors have specific planned comparisons against control and an expected ordering of interventions, but they condition follow-up tests on a significant omnibus interaction. This gatekeeping approach can be underpowered for targeted contrasts and is not aligned with the stated hypotheses. Conversely, if all pairwise comparisons are conducted after a significant omnibus test without multiplicity control, Type I error remains a concern.
issues.quote: The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if ... smaller in the group in which this method was applied than in the control group. In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed.

issues.subcategory: Exclusion of participants not exposed to co-witness details may induce bias
issues.description: Participants who do not hear any misleading information from the partner will be excluded. Exposure is partly a post-randomization outcome of discussion dynamics and memory, and may itself be affected by dyad characteristics or intervention timing/counterbalancing. Excluding such participants can bias estimates and reduce generalizability. At minimum, exposure criteria should be prespecified at item level and modeled rather than excluding entire participants where possible.
issues.quote: participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.

issues.subcategory: Mutual misinformation not guaranteed for all items
issues.description: The design assumes participants introduce mutual misinformation during discussion, but partners may agree, fail to mention the critical detail, give 'don't know,' or guess the other participant's correct detail. This means discussed items do not uniformly contain misinformation exposure. The proposed within-subject factor 'discussed vs non-discussed' may therefore misclassify exposure unless analyses are item-specific and conditional on actual co-witness statements.
issues.quote: participants discuss half of the dissimilar details they have seen, therefore they introduce mutual misinformation. ... However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading.

issues.subcategory: Transcription and discussion coding procedures unspecified
issues.description: The analysis depends on determining whether the partner provided misleading information and whether answers were disputed or non-disputed, based on audio recordings. The manuscript does not describe transcription procedures, coder blinding, reliability, treatment of inaudible speech, interruptions, simultaneous speech, or disagreements about coding.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded. ... if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave different answers during the discussion of a given item, their answers will be classified as disputed.

issues.subcategory: Disputed/non-disputed coding does not capture individual awareness or social influence
issues.description: The proposed disputed/non-disputed classification is based on overt disagreement during discussion. A participant may notice a discrepancy but remain silent, agree socially despite awareness, not encode the partner's answer, or later infer discrepancy from the warning. Thus this coding is an imperfect proxy for the theorized construct of discrepancy awareness and may mislead moderation analyses.
issues.quote: if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave different answers during the discussion of a given item, their answers will be classified as disputed ... if Participant A gave an answer ... and Participant B agreed with it or did not give an answer it will be classified as “non-disputed”.

issues.subcategory: Potential contamination between paired participants during interventions
issues.description: Participants remain in pairs through intervention phases, including feedback about the DRM task and podcasts telling them about partner misinformation. It is unclear whether they listen individually or together, whether they can interact during/after interventions, or whether one participant's reactions influence the other. This may increase dyadic dependence and introduce uncontrolled social effects during the intervention.
issues.quote: The procedure will consist of four main phases ... the participants (always a pair of them) ... Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast ... Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback

issues.subcategory: No details on preventing communication before final test
issues.description: After the intervention and before/during the individual final memory test, the manuscript does not specify whether participants are separated, monitored, or instructed not to communicate. Any continued communication could contaminate individual responses and undermine the interpretation as an individual memory test.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test of the original material

issues.subcategory: No assessment of suspicion about MORI deception before intervention
issues.description: Participants may notice that the partner saw a different version during the collaborative discussion, particularly when discrepancies arise. The study only asks about the real purpose at the end, after explicit warnings in some conditions. Without assessing suspicion before the intervention, it is impossible to know whether baseline suspicion differs across dyads or drives responses.
issues.quote: the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded

issues.subcategory: Post-treatment suspicion assessment confounded with intervention
issues.description: The suspicion/hypothesis-guessing measure is administered after interventions that intentionally reveal aspects of the deception in at least the Extended warning condition. Therefore, end-of-study guesses are partly caused by the manipulation and cannot validly identify preexisting awareness or invalid participants. Excluding based on this measure removes participants for successfully receiving the treatment.
issues.quote: In addition, the podcast will explain why the deception was applied. ... Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded

issues.subcategory: Intervention may change response criterion rather than memory conformity
issues.description: Warnings and memory fallibility education may induce participants to withhold answers, provide more 'other' responses, or lower confidence rather than improve resistance to misinformation. Because 'overall number of answers' is only one of several exploratory indices and no criterion/sensitivity framework is specified, reductions in misinformation-consistent answers could be misinterpreted as improved memory accuracy.
issues.quote: It has been assumed that as a result of giving such an extensive warning, participants would become more careful, alert, skeptical and cautious in their judgments ... Four indices will be derived ... (3) other answers ... (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: Final memory test items not provided
issues.description: The manuscript does not include the 20 final open-ended questions or the 12 collaborative questions and response options. Without these materials, reviewers cannot evaluate wording, leading questions, equivalence across discussed/non-discussed sets, cueing of critical details, or replicability.
issues.quote: The test will comprise 12 questions ... Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed ... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details

issues.subcategory: Intervention scripts/podcasts not provided
issues.description: The interventions are described generally, but exact scripts, examples, wording, tone, and instructions are not provided. Since subtle wording differences in warnings and memory education can strongly affect suggestibility and demand characteristics, exact materials are necessary for evaluation and replication.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast ... participants’ motivation ... will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.subcategory: No fidelity checks for audio presentation and DRM administration
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition requires the experimenter to read word lists and provide feedback. The manuscript does not specify whether the DRM lists will be standardized recordings, whether delivery pace and pronunciation will be controlled, or how fidelity will be monitored. Experimenter variability can affect false recall and intervention potency.
issues.quote: It will consist of the participants listening to experimenter presenting lists of words from a common category

issues.subcategory: DRM materials underspecified
issues.description: The manuscript gives one example DRM list and critical lures but does not provide all four selected lists, their Polish validation, presentation rate, recall timing, scoring rules, or expected false recall rates. This limits evaluation of whether the manipulation reliably demonstrates memory fallibility.
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: Exploratory DRM predictor available only in one condition
issues.description: The analysis plan proposes using DRM procedure results as a predictor of MORI results, but only participants in the Demonstration and motivation condition complete the DRM task. This severely limits sample size, makes the predictor confounded with intervention condition, and changes the task by giving feedback. The plan lacks specification of the model and whether prediction is within-condition only.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.subcategory: No balance check or stratification for counterbalancing version across conditions
issues.description: Half of pairs discuss one set of critical details and half discuss another, but the manuscript does not specify that counterbalancing version will be balanced within each intervention condition. If one condition has more pairs assigned to a more memorable or more confusable item set, the intervention effect could be confounded with item set.
issues.quote: In order to counterbalance the discussed details, 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs.

issues.subcategory: No balance of film version/glasses side/order
issues.description: Each member of a dyad sees one of two film versions via polarized glasses. The manuscript does not specify how version assignment to participant, seating position, sex, dominance, or glasses type will be randomized/counterbalanced. Version-specific item salience or seating/projector artifacts could bias conformity estimates.
issues.quote: each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie.

issues.subcategory: MORI visual manipulation quality not verified
issues.description: The MORI technique depends on participants seeing only their assigned version. The manuscript does not describe calibration procedures, checks for ghosting/crosstalk between images, participant visual checks, head-tilt monitoring, or criteria for excluding participants who may see both images. Technical leakage would undermine the misinformation manipulation.
issues.quote: Polarizing filters will be placed in front of the lens of each projector: one will be oriented vertically and the other horizontally. Moreover, each participant will receive polarizing glasses that will block one of the two possible versions of the movie.

issues.subcategory: Collaborative recognition format may alter natural memory conformity
issues.description: Participants discuss forced-choice recognition questions with five alternatives for 60 seconds each, which may prompt attention to specific critical details and constrain possible answers. This is different from natural co-witness conversation and may produce conformity through recognition-choice negotiation rather than spontaneous misinformation sharing. This limits construct validity for real eyewitness discussion.
issues.quote: The test will comprise 12 questions ... Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer.

issues.subcategory: Limited age range and recruitment population
issues.description: Participants are 16–35 and recruited via media/internet, likely producing a convenience sample. Eyewitnesses in real cases include children, older adults, diverse education levels, and people under stress. The manuscript motivates forensic implications but does not sufficiently acknowledge limits on generalizing to the broader eyewitness population.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: Low ecological validity of stimulus and setting
issues.description: Participants watch a silent 6.5-minute movie in a laboratory-like setting, discuss prompted details, and then receive explicit interventions immediately before a test. This differs from real crimes involving stress, emotion, variable viewing conditions, longer delays, repeated conversations, and investigative interviews. The manuscript claims closeness to real life and justice-system relevance without fully addressing these limitations.
issues.quote: the participants will watch a silent movie that lasts 6 minutes and 34 seconds. ... The main reason for that is that we wanted to make our research closer to real life settings.

issues.subcategory: Overstatement of intervention relevance to real interrogation
issues.description: The authors state that it is 'always possible' to undertake efforts just before interrogation, but in real cases investigators may not know whether or what co-witness misinformation occurred, and explicit warnings may be impractical or legally problematic. The causal effect in this controlled deception paradigm may not translate to forensic practice.
issues.quote: But it is always possible to undertake some efforts in order to prevent a witness from reporting misinformation just before the interrogation.

issues.subcategory: Normative influence dismissed too strongly
issues.description: The manuscript assumes normative impact has little use because the final test is individual, but conformity can persist due to earlier public commitment, desire to maintain agreement, anticipated evaluation, or internalized social pressure. The design does not measure or rule out normative influence. Dismissing it may lead to an overly narrow theoretical interpretation.
issues.quote: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing

issues.subcategory: Inoculation theory applied imprecisely
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention is described as based on inoculation theory, but the DRM task does not expose participants to a weakened form of the specific persuasive/social influence message they must resist, nor does it train discrimination between legitimate and illegitimate co-witness information. The theoretical mapping from persuasion inoculation to memory conformity is incomplete.
issues.quote: This was inspired by existing research on resisting social influence ... based on the inoculation theory ... The demonstration of the fallibility of memory will be done by means of the DRM technique

issues.subcategory: Contradictory predictions about memory fallibility education
issues.description: The manuscript predicts education about memory fallibility will reduce conformity by improving monitoring, but also acknowledges it may decrease confidence and increase suggestibility. This is a plausible alternative, but the theory does not specify conditions under which either effect should dominate or how competing mechanisms will be tested.
issues.quote: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility ... If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible.

issues.subcategory: Confidence ratings not integrated into analysis plan
issues.description: Participants rate confidence for each answer, but the analysis plan does not specify hypotheses, scoring, calibration analyses, or how confidence will be used. Given that confidence is central to the theoretical rationale, failing to analyze it or define its role is a missed opportunity and a reporting gap.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100% ...

issues.subcategory: Metamemory construct not measured
issues.description: Education about memory is theorized to increase metamemory, memory monitoring, efficacy, or affect, but no metamemory measure is included. Therefore, the study cannot establish that the intervention affected the construct it is intended to manipulate.
issues.quote: We assume that the lecture will also enhance memory monitoring, sense of memory efficacy or even memory-related affect.

issues.subcategory: Repeated-measures correlation estimate may not apply to modified outcome
issues.description: The power analysis assumes r = 0.07 between discussed and non-discussed repeated measures based on prior studies, but the planned study changes the final test format to open-ended responses and may score actual exposure differently. The repeated-measures correlation for the new outcome may differ substantially, affecting power.
issues.quote: A correlation r = 0.07 between repeated measures was assumed based on the research described above ... In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.

issues.subcategory: Power not adjusted for exclusions/replacement process
issues.description: The planned sample size is 240 analyzed participants, but exclusions are anticipated for technical problems, no exposure, and hypothesis guessing. Although the authors say excluded participants will be replaced for hypothesis guessing, they do not discuss replacement for all exclusions, recruitment burden, or how exclusions affect randomization balance and power. Differential exclusions may reduce effective power and bias estimates.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people ... If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person ... We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems ... participants who are not exposed ... will be excluded

issues.subcategory: Unequal experimenter contact across conditions
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition includes experimenter-administered DRM lists and individualized feedback, whereas other conditions appear to involve passive podcast listening. Experimenter contact, interpersonal authority, and feedback may influence motivation, suspicion, or compliance independently of the intended manipulation.
issues.quote: It will consist of the participants listening to experimenter presenting lists of words ... The results will be fed back to participants ... Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast

issues.subcategory: No control for prior memory/psychology knowledge
issues.description: Interventions involve education about misinformation, source monitoring, DRM, and memory fallibility. Participants with prior psychology training may already know these effects or recognize the DRM paradigm/MORI deception, affecting susceptibility and hypothesis guessing. The manuscript does not screen or measure this.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study ... will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: No preregistration or registered-report details for analytic decisions
issues.description: The manuscript appears intended as a Stage 1 registered report, but many key analytic decisions remain unspecified, including primary outcome, coding rules, exclusion coding, model specification, covariates, correction for multiple tests, and handling of clustering. Without these details, preregistration would not sufficiently constrain researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: If the Stage 1 review is accepted, the resubmission should be completed no later than in 2023.

issues.subcategory: Incorrect wording suggests empirical results before study completion
issues.description: The statement that empirical results may determine overlap is forward-looking, but the sentence contains a logical/grammatical error ('this does mean' likely intended 'does not mean'), which reverses the intended interpretation and creates conceptual ambiguity about whether equal effects imply equal mechanisms.
issues.quote: even if they produce the same results, this does mean that the mechanisms by which the were effective are always the same.

issues.subcategory: No description of compensation or incentives
issues.description: The manuscript does not report whether participants are compensated, receive course credit, or have incentives for accuracy. Motivation can influence memory effort and response criterion, especially in a study explicitly attempting to motivate accuracy.
issues.quote: they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: Accuracy motivation may differ across conditions
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition explicitly emphasizes the importance of accurate testimony and encourages reliance on own memory. The control and other interventions may not receive equivalent accuracy motivation. Any superiority of this condition may reflect increased task motivation rather than the demonstration of vulnerability or resistance to influence.
issues.quote: the participants’ motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast with information that inaccurate testimony are the main causes of erroneous court judgments ... The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory

issues.subcategory: Education and warning labels overlap with control of source credibility
issues.description: The Extended warning condition discredits the partner/source by explaining that the partner saw a different version, while Education about memory discusses general memory errors without source-specific discrediting. Thus intervention differences may reflect source discrediting specificity rather than warning length, education, or memory knowledge, complicating interpretation.
issues.quote: Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied ... Education about memory ... discussing the mechanisms of memory

issues.subcategory: No plan for checking assumptions of ANOVA
issues.description: The planned ANOVA requires assumptions including approximate normality of residuals, homogeneity of variance, and independence. The manuscript does not mention diagnostic checks, transformations, robust alternatives, or nonparametric/generalized models if assumptions are violated. Given bounded count outcomes and clustering, assumptions are likely problematic.
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.subcategory: Filler tasks may differentially interact with conditions but are not justified
issues.description: The study includes a 15-minute logic-puzzle filler and a 5-minute multiplication filler. The cognitive load, stress, and individual differences in mathematical/logical ability could affect mood or fatigue before interventions and memory test. The purpose and standardization of these tasks are not described, nor whether performance is recorded or controlled.
issues.quote: After watching the video, the participants will be engaged in a filler task (solving logic puzzles) for 15 minutes. ... another filler task: the participants will be asked to work on multiplication problems for five minutes.

issues.subcategory: No language/translation validation for intervention materials
issues.description: The film materials are said to have been translated into Polish, but the newly created podcasts, DRM lists, instructions, and final open-ended questions are not described as translated/back-translated or validated. This matters because wording and semantic associations are central to memory and DRM effects.
issues.quote: the set of materials used in the MORI technique has been successfully translated into Polish ... The extended warning will take the form ... The training will take the form ... Four lists will be chosen

issues.subcategory: Ignoring multinomial dependence among response categories
issues.description: Correct, misinformation-consistent, other, and no-answer/overall answer counts are mutually dependent categories from the same items. Running separate ANOVAs on each index ignores this dependence and can produce incoherent results. A multinomial or categorical mixed-effects model would better reflect the response process.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived ... the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ... and (4) the overall number of answers. ... using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices

issues.subcategory: No handling of participants wearing corrective or polarized glasses issues
issues.description: MORI depends on polarizing glasses fitting over corrective glasses and maintaining orientation. The manuscript quotes instructions but does not describe screening for participants whose glasses, visual impairments, or head tilt may compromise image separation or detail perception.
issues.quote: If you already wear glasses, the acuity glasses should fit over the top ... We find that people often see best when they keep their head straight rather than tilted

issues.subcategory: Misleading classification differs from stated discussed/non-discussed ANOVA
issues.description: The analysis plan first says the within-subject factor is discussed versus non-discussed items, but then states that only partner answers inconsistent with the participant's version will be classified as misleading. It is unclear whether the ANOVA uses all discussed items, only actually misleading discussed items, or item-level exposure classifications. These are different estimands and can yield different results.
issues.quote: one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) ... each answer given by the partner ... that is inconsistent with what the participant was presented with is misleading ... if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading

issues.subcategory: No plan for unequal number of misleading items per participant
issues.description: Because actual misinformation exposure depends on what the partner says, participants may have different numbers of misleading items. The proposed count/difference ANOVA does not explain how accuracy or misinformation rates will be computed when denominators vary, or whether participants with few exposures are weighted equally to those with many exposures.
issues.quote: if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading.

issues.subcategory: Potential confounding by co-witness discussion quality
issues.description: The amount, confidence, and persuasiveness of misinformation delivered by the partner will vary across dyads and items. Since these features are not standardized or modeled, differences in final memory may be attributable to variability in the social interaction rather than interventions. Audio coding could quantify exposure strength, but no plan is provided.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: Immediate intervention and final test limit delay generalization
issues.description: The intervention is administered shortly after the co-witness discussion and the memory test follows immediately. Real eyewitness interviews may occur hours, days, or weeks after events and discussions. The study cannot determine whether intervention effects persist over meaningful delays.
issues.quote: After the discussion, there will be another filler task ... for five minutes. After that, the third phase will take place ... Immediately after the participants are done ... they will complete the individual memory test

issues.subcategory: No participant flow plan
issues.description: The manuscript lacks a planned CONSORT-style flow description: number recruited, paired, randomized, excluded for each reason, replaced, analyzed per condition, and item-level missing/exposure counts. Given multiple exclusions and dyadic testing, a flow plan is important for transparency.
